node.label: Eugen Weber
node.date_label: Peasants into Frenchmen (1976) · France: Fin de Siècle (1986) · The Hollow Years (1994)
node.description: A historian of modern France whose Peasants into Frenchmen interprets national integration as a late and uneven transformation. Maurice Agulhon’s substantive review recognizes the combination of transport, markets, schooling and military service, while questioning the weight assigned to deliberate republican intervention.

proposed_edges.relationship: Interprets French national belonging as historically produced through uneven rural integration.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Agulhon’s substantive review843reports the thesis and questions its political periodization; not automatic adoption of the modernization label.

proposed_edges.relationship: Combines markets and transport with schools and conscription as mechanisms of rural transformation.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Agulhon credits the plural account while asking whether deliberate state integration is given too much weight; the critique remains explicit.
